claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about your circumstances. Let me begin with a few questions.

**First, could you tell me the name(s) of the child or children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I'm asking about my child Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about your child **Alex**.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about Alex's circumstances.

**Can you tell me Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex just turned 17 a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 17 years old.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex currently in work or receiving any benefits?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has actually started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that Alex has started an apprenticeship.

**Can you tell me a bit more about the apprenticeship - is it a paid apprenticeship, and approximately how many hours per week is Alex working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a paid apprenticeship. Alex doesn't work full-time though - it's less than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's helpful to know.

**Are you the person who is responsible for Alex - for example, are you Alex's parent or guardian, and are you living with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**One more question: Are you a British citizen, or do you have the right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and have the right to be here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me consider the rules carefully:

- **Alex's age**: At 17 years old, Alex is within the eligible age range (Child Benefit can be claimed for children up to age 19 if they're in approved education or training)
- **Alex's apprenticeship**: Alex is in an approved apprenticeship, which is a form of approved training
- **Hours worked**: Alex works less than 24 hours per week, which is within the permitted threshold (apprentices can work up to 24 hours per week and still qualify)
- **Your relationship**: You are Alex's parent living with Alex
- **Residency**: You have the right to reside in the UK

Based on these circumstances, Alex meets the criteria for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex meets all the requirements because:
- Alex is 17 and in approved apprenticeship training
- Alex works less than 24 hours per week (within the permitted limit)
- You are Alex's parent living with Alex in the UK

You should be able to proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you need any further assistance or have questions about the claims process itself, please let me know!
